newsitem.title: KENYA: Zaire rebel leader denies refugee killings.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel leader denies refugee killings.

text.p: Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila on Wednesday dismissed as "total nonsense" reports that his forces had slaughtered Rwandan Hutu refugees at a camp south of Kisangani on Tuesday.

Kabila, head of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL), told Reuters by telephone from Zaire's second largest city Lubumbashi that refugees had attacked villagers and his army only stepped in to stop the fighting.
Kabila blamed the United Nations for the chaos in Kisangani, saying the world body had failed to ease the plight of the refugees, many of whom he said were former soldiers and militia.

"It is absolute nonsense. There is no truth whatsoever in these reports. The truth is that local Zaireans were attacked by the Rwandan Hutu militia and our army only stepped in to stop the fighting," Kabila said.

"The United Nations and its refugee agency has disastrously failed to address the issue of the refugees. They are responsible for the chaos in Kisangani today. It is a question of gross inefficiency, misplaced priorities and indecision on part of the U.N.," Kabila added.
Kabila, whose forces now control about half of Africa's third largest country, said he would be taking up the matter with United Nations authorities.
"Maybe this can only be resolved by talking to the highest authority in the United Nations instead of these incompetent fellows in Kisangani," he said.
Zairean villagers said on Wednesday that Kabila's rebels slaughtered many Rwandans at a camp south of the northeastern capital of Kisangani on Tuesday in revenge for the killing of six villagers.
The villagers said a pitched battle between rebels and refugees accompanied the slaughter on Tuesday at camps near Kasese village, 25 km (15 miles) south of Kisangani.
"The (rebel) army went to the camp at 8 a.m. yesterday. They killed many, many refugees -- hundreds. There was lots of shooting all morning," Alphonse Soku, a farmer, told Reuters.
"They used a mechanical digger to bury the bodies."
The U.N. refugee agency said earlier on Wednesday it was checking reports that the refugees had fled after a rebel military operation on Tuesday and attacks by local villagers.

Kabila said also that the UNHCR had failed to honour promises of an airlift for the refugees and the alliance had in turn refused to have them transported by road because many of them were diseased by cholera and posed a threat to local Zaireans.

"The United Nations has failed despite repeated promises to airlift these people. They now say they have no aircraft and they want them to move by road, but how can we allow diseased people to move freely through Kisangani and how do we control them especially that many of them are hardcore criminals," he said.
On Sunday rebel authorities in Kisangani refused to allow the U.N. to press ahead with an airlift because of the cholera outbreak.
The refugees fled Rwanda in 1994 and are collectively accused by minority Tutsis of genocide in Rwanda in the same year.
They arrived at their Kasese camps in mid-March after six months of trekking over volcanic rock and through bush and jungle in a vain attempt to flee the Tutsi-backed rebels.
Kabila bowed to international pressure on April 5 and agreed to an airlift to repatriate 100,000 Rwandan refugees at Kasese and further south towards Ubundu. But it has failed to start.
Angry Zaireans blocked aid workers and journalists from reaching Kasese on Monday and Tuesday and looted food aid.
